chunks: Muhammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Rifāʿah ibn Mūsā al-Nakhkhās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"If a man divorces his wife, and she claims that the belongings are hers while he claims that the belongings are his, then he is entitled to what belongs to men, and she is entitled to what belongs to women."
And it has also been narrated: "The woman has a greater right to the belongings, because those within her region may know that a woman brings belongings with her to her husband's house."

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: more entitled; having the stronger right or claim
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the husband or man in the legal dispute
key_terms.الْمَتَاعَ: household belongings or personal effects in dispute
key_terms.امْرَأَتَهُ: his wife, the other party in the claim
key_terms.زَوْجِهَا: her husband, whose house she enters with belongings
key_terms.طَلَّقَ: divorced; the act of terminating the marriage

ai.seo_question: How are household belongings divided between husband and wife after divorce in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal dispute over household belongings after divorce. It states that items commonly associated with men go to the husband and items associated with women go to the wife, while another transmitted report notes that the wife may have a stronger claim because women are known to bring belongings into the marital home.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3430 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Rifa'ah ibn Musa al-Nakhkhas, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"If a man divorces his wife, and she claims that the belongings are hers while he claims that the belongings are his, then the man is entitled to what is for men, and the woman is entitled to what is for women."

It has also been narrated:
"The woman has a greater right to the belongings because it is commonly known among the people of the area that a woman brings belongings with her to her husband's house."
